interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The postoperative pathology demonstrated favorable findings regarding local disease control. The surgical pathology report noted, "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 4+4 (ISUP grade group 4), pathological stage pT2. There was no extraprostatic extension; surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." This suggests a low risk for local recurrence based on negative margins and absence of seminal vesicle invasion.

The preoperative findings included a biopsy identifying Gleason 4+4 carcinoma. The absence of lymph node metastasis is a reassuring finding. However, the status of the nodes was documented as negative, which supports the surgical findings. The prognosis is tempered by the lack of recorded postoperative PSA and its trajectory, as "Postoperative PSA and its trajectory are needed; pathology alone does not establish biochemical recurrence." Missing postoperative PSA information significantly widens the uncertainty regarding biochemical recurrence. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent trajectory would be crucial in revising the prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 33.91 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 27.13–40.70 months; its coverage has not been validated.

This is countered by the biopsy finding of "Gleason 4+4 (ISUP grade group 4, AI model-predicted ISUP 4) was identified in the right side; cribriform pattern and intraductal carcinoma were present." The absence of lymph node metastasis is a positive finding. The preoperative PSA was 4.8. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, meaning biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. The documented negative margins and absence of seminal vesicle invasion are favorable prognostic factors. Missing nodal sampling is not applicable as nodes were sampled and no metastasis was found. Information regarding the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory is crucial for revising the prognosis.
